newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU formally approves high-tech trade deal.
newsitem.headline: EU formally approves high-tech trade deal.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers formally approved on Monday the global Information Technology Agreement (ITA), which will phase out tariffs on a range of computer and telecoms equipment by the year 2000.
The ministers asked the European Commission to make minor changes to the EU's text and to submit it to the World Trade Organisation in Geneva, EU officials said.

The deal, agreed in Singapore in December, will cut tariffs in four stages between 1997 and 2000. The participants -- the 15-member EU and some 20 other countries -- aim to formally conclude the accord by April 1.
Those countries represent more than 90 percent of trade in information technology products, the "critical mass" that the EU and United States said was necessary for implementation of the accord.
The first tariff cuts will take place in July. Some developing countries will be allowed to delay cuts for some products until after 2000.
